A survey from YouGov/Economist released on Tuesday shows that in a generic congressional vote, 36 percent of U.S. adults would pick the Democratic candidate compared to 31 percent who would pick the Republican candidate. One percent said other, eight percent said not sure and 23 percent said they would not vote.

The poll surveyed 1,592 U.S. adults from August 28-31 and had a margin of error of 3.5 percent. [...] A Quantus Insights poll shows that among 1,200 likely voters, 49.7 percent would pick Democrats in the generic congressional ballot compared to 42.8 percent for Republicans and 7.5 percent were undecided. results.content: Other recent surveys have also pointed to a Democratic advantage on the generic congressional ballot. A YouGov/Economist poll found that 36 per cent of US adults would choose a Democratic candidate, compared with 31 per cent for a Republican candidate. [...] A separate Quantus Insights survey of likely voters put Democrats ahead 49.7 per cent to 42.8 per cent on the generic congressional ballot. The same poll showed Democrats leading Republicans 49.3 per cent to 43.4 per cent in a generic Senate ballot.
results.title: Republicans Face Fresh Midterm Warning as Democrats Gain Party Identification Edge

results.content:
And here’s why it matters.

The new Economist/YouGov poll has Democrats leading the House vote among likely voters:

Democrats 49%  
Republicans 38%

D+11.

But this is NOT your typical generic-ballot poll.

As election analyst G. Elliott Morris pointed out this morning, YouGov asked voters using the NAMES OF THE ACTUAL CANDIDATES RUNNING IN THEIR DISTRICT. [...] Yet the national generic congressional ballot has generally been sitting around D+6 or D+7.

Why the difference?

Maybe we’re beginning to see part of the answer.

The generic ballot is abstract.

“Democrat or Republican for Congress?”
